title: AST Node Classes: Literals, Variables, Operations, and Control
description: Defines 10 AST node classes using dataclass: Num, Bool, Var, BinOp, IfExpr, Let, LetRec, Fun, App. Each has a line field for error reporting. Nodes represent literals, variables, binary operations, conditionals, let bindings, recursive let, functions, and application. Base for parser and evaluator.

steps.description: Imports: dataclass for node definitions, field for defaults, Optional and List from typing.
Literal and variable nodes: Num(value:int), Bool(value:bool), Var(name:str). Each has line:int=0 for source location tracking.
BinOp(op:str, left:object, right:object) for binary operations. IfExpr(cond:object, then_:object, else_:object) for conditionals. Both carry line field.
Let(name:str, value:object, body:object) for local bindings. LetRec(name:str, value:object, body:object) for recursive bindings (functions that can call themselves).
Fun(param:str, body:object) for function abstraction. App(func:object, arg:object) for function application. Core of first-class functions.
All 10 node classes share the line:int=0 field. This uniform design lets the evaluator and error reporting treat source locations consistently across every expression type.

steps.question: Why do Let and LetRec both have name, value, and body fields if they mean different things?
steps.answer: The structure is the same: bind name to value, evaluate body in extended environment. The difference is semantic: Let evaluates value in the old environment, LetRec evaluates value in the new environment where name is already bound (enabling recursion). Same AST shape, different evaluation rule.
